featured_reviews.name: Aayush Jayswal
featured_reviews.review_text:
My friend and I recently attended an art workshop at Shobha's Art Studio in Bandra West, and it was an unforgettable experience! The workshop, led by Shobha herself, offered a perfect balance of creativity, technique, and fun.

We explored two styles during the session -- I did the "landscape canvas painting" and my friend tried the "impasto knife painting". Shobha's guidance was exceptional -- she explained each technique with clarity, making it easy for us(especially me as I was kind of a beginner for this😅). Her passion for art was evident, and she made sure that we felt comfortable expressing our unique style.

The landscape canvas painting segment allowed me to play with colors and perspective, creating serene and vibrant scenes.
The impasto knife painting was a completely different but equally enjoyable experience, as  it showed how to use texture to bring artwork to life.

Shobha was patient and encouraging, ensuring we left with pieces we were proud of(and yessss we did!!!).❤️

Overall, it was a wonderfully creative and relaxing day, and we would highly recommend Shobha's workshops to anyone looking to explore their artistic side. Whether you're a beginner or a seasoned artist, this experience is worth it!💯

Here's a glimpse of the artwork we made...

featured_reviews.name: Abhishek Bhoite
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Bombay Art Society's contemporary architecture from the outside is pretty iconic, but it is in ruins from the inside. The maintenance of the gallery is below par. The staircase is a piece of art in itself.

There is a ramp at the main entrance for wheelchairs, but the restrooms inside the building are not accessible & very shabbily made.

This is an excellent example of how the architect's vision has been destroyed by the people & contractors who run the place. The gallery definitely has a lot of scope to develop in the future.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Before writing such review, you should at least get some basic information about public art institution serving society at large and promting art and artists. We don't know what time of the year you visited but just after COVID the art galleries condition was bit of an issue due to rainwater leakage; due to leakage, some part of false ceiling was collapsed during lockdown, place was bit moist, and it took bit of a time to fix it. It is fixed long back, and all three galleries are functioning and there are regular exhibitions taking place in the galleries; not only that but community art classes also started; our auditorium is functioning. 
Washroom cleaning was small issue immediately after COVID and is taken care now, as there is ample staff. 
The structure is architecturally beautiful from outside; it is the same architect who has designed it from inside too. 
The place is run by the managing committee consisting of artists and art writers and contractor have no role after building is completed. The Bombay Art Society is one of the oldest art institutions in Asia promoting art and artists; Society is always run by committee for 135 years since 1888; committee is elected every three/five years by society's life members. This complex is new, and every new art space takes time to build its own audience. 
Please don't spread misinformation based on single visit. Hope, you will visit our art galleries when you are in the area. 
The Bombay Art Society Team

Thank you, for making this holiday season so memorable and creatively enriching for our daughter!!

name: Bollywood Art Project
description: Bollywood Art Project (B.A.P) is an urban public art project that aims to transform the walls of Mumbai into a living memorial to Bollywood legends. We would love to reach where Bollywood lovers are. We have painted India's tallest mural of Amitabh Bachchan. 230 feet High, and India’s biggest mural of Dadasaheb Phalke on MTNL Building in Bandra (W) Mumbai

featured_reviews.name: Vignesh Balaji
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Bollywood Art Project (BAP) is a vibrant tribute to Mumbai’s rich cinematic history, transforming the city’s streets into an open-air gallery of stunning Bollywood-inspired murals. Located primarily in Bandra, these larger-than-life artworks celebrate legendary actors, iconic movie moments, and the essence of Indian cinema.

Each mural is meticulously crafted, capturing the expressions, colors, and nostalgia of Bollywood’s golden era. From Amitabh Bachchan’s towering presence to Madhubala’s timeless charm, every piece tells a story that resonates with movie lovers and art enthusiasts alike. The detailing and scale of the murals make them a visual delight and a must-visit for photographers and Instagrammers.

Beyond just art, BAP serves as a cultural movement, blending Mumbai’s love for cinema with street art. Walking through the painted lanes of Bandra, one can truly appreciate how Bollywood is not just an industry but an emotion for millions.

If you’re in Mumbai, taking a stroll through the Bollywood Art Project is a unique and immersive way to experience the city’s artistic and cinematic soul. Highly recommended! 🎥🎨✨

featured_reviews.review_text: I spent a truly fantastic 4-5 hours with Ranjit at the end of November 2023. Quite by chance, I found his project through Google search and he agreed to meet up with me. I was staying at an Airbnb on Chapel Road, near his studio. He's an incredibly talented guy, who's passionate about his work and he's SO friendly and he took me to see several of his awesome murals. I even went with him to the unveiling of a mural for an Indian Netflix movie that dropped on the streaming service today (26/12/23). He's not one for the limelight, but credit where credit's due - he's done/is doing some incredible work. Thanks Ranjit, it was really great to meet you and chat with you. Keep up your great work. 👍 🎨 🎊 Best regards from Sue!
